audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 fits a 47.82% WR over 4019 games: Viktor out-ranges early, Ryze flips it on items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart disagrees with the content layer and packet on rows 1-6 (full had Viktor/Viktor/Viktor/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill; content and packet both say Viktor/Skill/Ryze/Viktor/Viktor/Ryze/Ryze).
audit.why: Content and packet agree; full layer carried a stale chart. Level 3 pre-augment is Ryze's window (E-W Flux root + Q-E-Q), 4-6 swing to Viktor on augments and Arcane Storm, items flip it back.
audit.corrected: phases[1..6].side moved to Skill/Ryze/Viktor/Viktor/Ryze/Ryze with matching whys and ratings; win[] already correct so no content chart edits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content called Viktor's R 'Chaos Storm' (stale name — kit says Arcane Storm), labelled Gravity Field as (E) when it is his W, and called the stun an 'E stun'. Neither layer stated that Arcane Storm is an interruptible channel that Ryze's Rune Prison cancels, nor the Siphon Power auto-reset burst tell.
audit.why: Kit file: W is Gravity Field (17/16/15/14/13s), E is Hextech Ray (12-8s), R is Arcane Storm (120/100/80s, channel flag: any CC cancels). Missing-interactions file lists both the channel-cancel and the auto-reset tell for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Names and slots fixed across content; Rune Prison-cancels-Arcane-Storm added to spikes[1], dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.cooldowns; auto-reset tell added to breakdown.early.

audit.why: Lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT; kit gives Gravity Field 17s rank 1, Hextech Ray 12s, Rune Prison 11s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d referenced 'a Zed mark' in a Viktor matchup — copy bleed from another lane opponent.

edits.before: W online: the point-blank root answers anyone who closes. Trade Q-W-Q only when his engage tool is down.
edits.after: W online, but it only roots through Flux — his Q shield blanks short pokes, so trades stay even until 3.

edits.before: Viktor
edits.after: Ryze

edits.before: E unlocks the real combo: E-Q flux chunks and the wave-bounce clears. The lane starts being yours to play.
edits.after: E unlocks the real combo: E-W roots through Flux, then Q-E-Q chunks him before his augments arrive. Your window.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Tear + Lost Chapter and the EQ machine hums — short-trade his every wave contact and walk away before the answer.
edits.after: His augments land: the bigger Q shield blanks your short trades and Hextech Ray shoves. Give ground and keep farming.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Realm Warp online — you are now a map play waiting to happen. The lane is a timer: shove and warp somewhere profitable.
edits.after: His 6 is stronger in lane: Arcane Storm plus Gravity Field owns the all-in. Save Realm Warp for the map, not this duel.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ryze

edits.before: RoA spike: your combo chunks half bars and your root starts kill chains. Force the trades you spent five levels avoiding.
edits.after: RoA spike: E-Q chunks half bars and the Flux root starts kill chains. Force the trades you spent five levels avoiding.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ryze

edits.before: Two items and you ARE the win condition: EQ deletes carries, W stops divers, and Realm Warp turns objectives into ambushes.
edits.after: Two items and you ARE the win condition: EQ deletes carries, the Flux root stops divers, Realm Warp ambushes objectives.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rune Prison has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Gravity Field (W): 17s at rank 1, 13s max — when it drops you have that long to fight on your terms. - Hextech Ray (E): 12s early; step up after he lasers the wave. - Your Rune Prison (11s) cancels his Arcane Storm channel outright — hold it for exactly that moment.

edits.before: Farm the Tear, hold the root, dodge the headline spell. Ryze early is a savings account — deposits only.
edits.after: Farm the Tear and dodge Hextech Ray; his combo opens with a Q auto-reset — the auto wind-up is your cue out.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Every max-range Q is a free Tear deposit — his Siphon Power is 600 range to your 1000, so farm from where he cannot answer.

edits.before: E the wave, Q the flux bounce, and W-root if he steps to answer — three-spell trades that end before his combo starts.
edits.after: Hextech Ray is 12s at rank 1 — when he spends it on the wave or whiffs it, the E-Q trade is free for most of that window.

edits.before: Your root is your only 'stop' button — a W spent poking is a Zed mark you can't answer.
edits.after: His Siphon Power is 600 range, your Q is 1000 — CS he pokes you for was farmable from safety.

edits.before: Spending W on poke and then face-tanking the engage it was born to stop — rootless Ryze is a Tear with a health bar.
edits.after: Rune Prison cancels his Arcane Storm channel mid-cast — spend it on poke and his 120s R runs its full course on you.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport, always — Ryze is a scaling map champion and TP doubles the thesis. Nothing else is defensible on him.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport, always — Ryze is a scaling map champion and TP extends the map game. Nothing else is defensible on him.

edits.before: Viktor favored: his augmented Q shield and Gravity Field (E) let him out-poke and zone you.
edits.after: Viktor favored: his augmented Q shield and Gravity Field (W) let him out-poke and zone you.

edits.before: Viktor favored: Chaos Storm (R) plus his E stun give him wave and fight control at 6.
edits.after: Viktor favored: Arcane Storm (R) plus his W stun give him wave and fight control at 6.

edits.before: Level 3 is your window: before Viktor upgrades his Gravity Field (E) you can walk up, W (Rune Prison) root him and land Q-E-Q for a real chunk. Once he hits 4-5 and augments his Siphon Power (Q) shield plus his laser E, he pushes the wave and out-pokes you, so cash your pressure at 3 before his augments come online.
edits.after: Level 3 is your window: before Viktor's augments arrive you can land Flux (E), W-root him through it and follow Q-E-Q for a real chunk. Once he hits 4-5 and augments his Siphon Power (Q) shield plus Hextech Ray (E), he pushes the wave and out-pokes you, so cash your pressure at 3 before the augments come online.

edits.before: Viktor's Chaos Storm (R) storm plus his Gravity Field (E) stun zone controls the fight; he will shove and look to combo you against the storm. Do not stand in his E line, respect the stun, and hold W to break his root chain rather than to engage.
edits.after: Viktor's Arcane Storm (R) plus his Gravity Field (W) stun zone controls the fight — but his R is a channel and your Rune Prison cancels it outright. Do not stand in the field, respect the stun, and hold W to break the storm rather than to engage.

edits.before: Both of you are late-game monsters, but a clean W root removes his ability to kite with Q shield and E stun, letting your Q-reset chain out-DPS him. Punish the window before his third augment and Rabadon's come online.
edits.after: Both of you are late-game monsters, but a clean W root removes his ability to kite with Q shield and W stun, letting your Q-reset chain out-DPS him. Punish the window before his third augment and Rabadon's come online.

edits.before: Level 3 is yours to punish before his augments, then 4-6 swing back to him as his augmented Q shield, Gravity Field (E) zone and Chaos Storm (R) let him poke and control the wave. Take your level 3 trade, then respect his poke and hold W to peel.
edits.after: Level 3 is yours to punish before his augments, then 4-6 swing back to him as his augmented Q shield, Gravity Field (W) zone and Arcane Storm (R) let him poke and control the wave. Take your level 3 trade, then respect his poke and hold W to peel.
